grounds:
Ground: the finding reads "a high risk flag" as "any of the four derived flags", but the spec sentence is "Route to the expensive model ONLY WHEN a step carries a high risk flag" (spec.md:196). The word "only" makes premium the exception. Reading all four as high inverts that sentence, because public-interface is derived by _TOP_LEVEL_MODULE_RE = ^ai_router/[^/]+\.py$ (approved_plan.py:59-61), which matches EVERY top-level module in the package. Every session in sets 142-147 touches at least one, this one included. Premium would therefore fire on essentially every plan, making the expensive model the default reviewer rather than the exception, and deleting the economy the set is built on: "free first, then cheap" (the session heading) and "Reviewing a plan is also far cheaper than reviewing a diff" (spec.md:9-11). A trigger that always fires is not a trigger; it is the default with extra steps.

The schema is the second half of the argument: approved-plan.schema.json enumerates exactly four risk_flags and labels none of them "high" (approved_plan.py:42-45 defines the same four). So "a high risk flag" cannot mean "any risk flag" without the qualifier doing no work. It requires a designated subset, and the code names that subset in exactly one place, HIGH_RISK_FLAGS (plan_review.py:63-71), with the reasoning stated as a constraint beside it.

The subset chosen is the narrow, expensive-to-get-wrong pair: sensitive-path (the router's own machine state, its schemas, and the config and lockfiles that decide what a session may do) and dependency-change (the dependency set under everything). Those are rare and consequential. public-interface and integration-module are neither: the first fires on nearly every step, and the second is derived from docs/modules.yaml, which this repository does not have at all, so it is inert here and escalating on it would widen the promise while changing nothing measurable.

Finally, set 146 is "measure-then-enable": it compares this path's cost against the current pipeline before the operator decides to enable it. A premium-by-default reviewer would poison that comparison before it is run, which is the one measurement this whole sequence exists to produce.

The two flags that mark a genuinely expensive mistake escalate. Nothing about the finding's failure scenario is a defect; it is the designed behavior of the sentence's "only".
